programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies watch some children learn about the number two. Dipsy and Laa-Laa are eating Tubby Toast. They play the game 'Two Little Teletubbies', but while they are playing the Noo-Noo tidies up their Tubby Toast.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies are eating Tubby Toast. They stop to watch Amy making pasta. A ball of string appears in Teletubbyland. Po knocks the string in to the air with her scooter and it makes a stringy mess all over Teletubbyland.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: Tinky Winky calls the other Tubbies to come and watch Tamzin Griffin pretend to be Funny Lady and tell the story about the naughty sock. The Tubby Toast machine makes a tower of tubby toast.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies watch some children looking at penguins waddling and swimming. In Teletubbyland, the Tubbies play walk fast and slow, far and near and other different ways.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies play 'Boo', but stop to watch Ned help his dad plant and water some geraniums. In Teletubbyland, nine pretty flowers and a watering can appear.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: Samira and her friends show the Teletubbies their gymnastic routines. The Teletubbies do their own gymnastics.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies watch Matthew and James help their uncle milk the cows. In Teletubbyland, the Tubby Custard machine isn't working, so they sing a special 'Tubby Custard' song. Then, the Tubby Custard machine works again.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: A voice trumpet appears and the Teletubbies dance, before watching two girls do some Flamenco dancing with their teacher. It's time for the Teletubbies to wash their feet. They love using their Tubby Sponges.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Tubbies watch a little boy peel and mash some eggs for an egg mayonnaise sandwich. The Teletubbies laugh when they make a tune whilst eating their Tubby Custard.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: Dipsy says "Eh-oh" and runs off to find the other Tubbies. They watch some children make fantastic animals from papermache.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Tubbies watch a little girl who loves monkeys help her mum feed them in a zoo. Tinky Winky sits down to eat some Tubby Toast.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: Tinky Winky says "Eh-oh". The Teletubbies and some children watch Tamzin Griffin pretend to be the Funny Lady and tell the story of the naughty hat. The Teletubbies are very happy when they find their favourite things to play with.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: In Teletubbyland, the Tubbies are trying to be quiet. They watch Oscar read the story of the Gingerbread Boy to his brother Felix. A voice trumpet appears and sings the nursery rhyme.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies dance an up and down dance. They watch some children painting pictures and patterns on to eggs. In Teletubbyland, Laa-Laa dances with her ball until the magical tree appears.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy and Laa-Laa sit down to eat some Tubby Custard. Po wants some too. She tries to eat the other's Tubby Custard, but they won't let her.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies watch a little boy show us how to make a Turban. The Tubbies go for a walk, but Po, Laa-Laa and Dipsy want to play with their favourite things.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: A voice trumpet rises and teaches the Teletubbies a nursery rhyme. Then they watch Becky go for a ride on a Tram. Po rides her scooter too fast and knocks the other Tubbies over.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)
programme.desc: The Teletubbies want to go to sleep, but Tinky Winky finds Po already asleep in his bed. So he goes to look for somewhere else to sleep.

programme.title: Teletubbies (Classic)

programme.title: The Other Side of History: Daily Life in the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Taking On the Other Side of History
programme.desc: The past comes alive when considering the imaginary lives of ordinary people; these include the citizens, soldiers and slaves who live on the other side of history; asking questions that many textbooks never ask.

programme.title: The Other Side of History: Daily Life in the Ancient World
programme.desc: Taking a look at the lives of human ancestors; picturing oneself as a Neanderthal, whose life is dominated by the environment; discovering the significance of the human mind, language and art in the Old Stone Age.

programme.title: Understanding Imperial China: Dynasties, Life, and Culture
programme.sub-title: Opium, Trade, and War in Imperial China
programme.desc: Examining opium, a pervasive symbol of late imperial China; the history of opium use; how opium is inextricably linked to imperial culture, society and economics; the British opium trade; the Opium Wars; Chinese measures to eradicate the drug.

programme.title: Understanding Imperial China: Dynasties, Life, and Culture
programme.desc: The story behind the famous terra-cotta warriors; daily life in the Qin Dynasty; encountering Emperor Qinshi Huangdi; his highly bureaucratic and technocratic regime; exploring the site of the terra-cotta army; how the clay figures are made.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
programme.desc: Exploring The French and Indian War of the mid-1700s, which is one of the formative conflicts in American military history; focusing on the experiences of Lt. Col. George Washington, a young colonial officer fighting for the British.

programme.title: American Military History: From Colonials to Counterinsurgents
programme.desc: When the colonies begin their struggle for independence, they choose George Washington to lead the army; Washington's defense of Boston; his defeat trying to hold New York City; contrasting British and American objectives in the Revolutionary War.

programme.title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
programme.sub-title: The Unknown Story of Ancient North America
programme.desc: Revealing the truths of ancient North America, which include pyramids, state-of-the-art highways and productive innovators; how the societies seemed destined to remain a mystery due to European conquerors and no written records.

programme.title: Ancient Civilizations of North America
programme.sub-title: The First Human Migrations to the Americas
programme.desc: DNA evidence pointing to Asia as the origin of all human migration to North America; migration passages across the Bering Strait; ancient habitation sites across the continent; why scientists cannot yet agree on the ages of the sites.

programme.title: The World of Biblical Israel
programme.sub-title: Biblical Israel - The Story of a People
programme.desc: Entering the world of biblical Israel with a historical overview; an examination of how the Bible gives insights into the daily life of ancient Israelites; considering the context for how the Bible comes into being.

programme.title: The World of Biblical Israel
programme.sub-title: By the Rivers of Babylon - Exile
programme.desc: A look at the Babylonian exile; the exiled Judeans begin asking themselves who they are as a people and why they are conquered; as the Bible begins to be compiled in this time of exile, it offers two vantage points for understanding its history.

programme.title: Sex in the Middle Ages

programme.title: Sex in the Middle Ages
programme.sub-title: Let's Talk about Medieval Sex, Baby

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance

programme.title: Great Artists of the Italian Renaissance
programme.desc: Around 1400, a European-wide style known as International Gothic flourishes in Italy; artists including Lorenzo Monaco and Gentile da Fabriano retain the style; others, such as Lorenzo Ghiberti, develop a new style that is known as Renaissance.

programme.title: Cooking Across the Ages

programme.title: Cooking Across the Ages

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.desc: The opening lecture presents the main themes of the course; beginning with the concept of total war; other themes include the role of ideology, the meanings ascribed to the war by different sides and the war's legacy.

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.desc: Examining the state of Europe and the world before the onset of the war in 1914; the emergence of the German Empire creates strains in the international balance of power; divided among Great Britain, France, Germany, Austria-Hungary and Russia.

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.sub-title: Towards Crisis in Politics and Culture
programme.desc: Even among those who expect war, there are widespread misconceptions about the nature of the conflict to come; in this lecture, exploring the prevailing ideas and attitudes in Europe; the premonitions noted by contemporaries of coming disaster.

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.sub-title: Causes of the War and the July Crisis, 1914
programme.desc: This lecture analyzes the immediate events that lead to war; the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary at Sarajevo in June 1914; the diplomatic chain reactions that follow in the July Crisis.

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.desc: The hysterical celebration known as the August Madness greets the outbreak of war between the Central Powers (Germany and Austria-Hungary) and the Allies (France, Great Britain and Russia); how widespread this emotional outburst really is.

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.sub-title: The Failed Gambles - War Plans Break Down
programme.desc: This lecture follows the unfolding of the German Schlieffen Plan, which envisions quick victory on two fronts; the French Plan XVII aims to recover lost French territories; both attempts are thwarted.

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.desc: The Western Front soon freezes into static trench warfare and horrific slaughter from attempts to break this deadlock; generals on both sides seek a breakthrough that allows sweeping offensives and glorious cavalry charges; these never materialize.

programme.title: World War I: The "Great War"
programme.sub-title: Life and Death in the Trenches
programme.desc: A detailed overview of the trench landscape from the perspective of ordinary soldiers; the elaborate fortifications; the omnipresence of death; the codes of behavior such as the Christmas fraternizations between the trenches in 1914.
